headline: Sales and margins expand sharply; debt charge dents profit
summary_short: Revenue rose 32.1% y/y to $1,945.5M and gross margin widened to 59.9% from 57.8%, while a $50.5M loss on debt extinguishment from redeeming all $800M of 6.750% senior secured notes weighed on net finance costs.
summary_long: Q1 revenue grew 32.1% y/y to $1,945.5M, led by Technical Apparel (+33.3%) and Outdoor Performance (+42.0%) on Arc'teryx and Salomon volume growth; DTC revenue rose 44.6% on an expanded store network. Gross margin widened 210bp to 59.9% on favorable channel, region and product mix, while SG&A rose 33.4% on DTC investment. Adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 22.2% from 20.3%. Net income attributable to equity holders rose to $164.6M despite a $50.5M loss on debt extinguishment from redeeming all $800M of 6.750% senior secured notes. Cash and equivalents were $683.7M, up from $422.1M a year earlier. Management guided FY2026 capex to approximately $400M.

drivers.explanation: Growth was broad-based across all three segments, primarily driven by Arc'teryx and Salomon volume growth in Technical Apparel and Outdoor Performance, plus a 44.6% DTC increase from an expanded retail network.
Margin expansion to 59.9% from 57.8% was "primarily driven by favorable channel, region, product and brand mix."
Gross-margin gains outpaced a 33.4% rise in SG&A tied to higher personnel, advertising, rent and D&A from DTC and Greater China/Asia Pacific expansion.
Operating-profit growth and a lower effective tax rate (29.3% vs 30.1%) more than offset a $50.5M loss on debt extinguishment from the notes redemption.
Not separately discussed in the release; EPS growth tracks the shard's net-income growth (SEC/Yahoo-sourced, not company-narrated).

Revenue, margin and profit growth reflect volume gains across Arc'teryx, Salomon and Wilson, partly offset by a one-time $50.5M debt-extinguishment charge from redeeming the company's senior secured notes.
